# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 16 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 16 | **Condition:** moderately preserved

---

**16:1** I thank You, O Lord, for You have not abandoned my lot in the congregation of deceit,

**16:2** and in the council of the hidden ones You have not placed my portion.

**16:3** But You have called me to Your grace, and to Your forgiveness [...]

**16:4** and in the abundance of Your mercies to all who return to You.

**16:5** For You have not set my judgment in the council of the secret ones,

**16:6** and You have not stored up truth for the way of the wicked.

**16:7** And I know that You have chosen me for [...] and that no one from the lips of the wicked will go astray from Your way.

**16:8** And I know that in Your hand is the fashioning of every spirit, and its activity You have established

**16:9** before You created it. How can anyone change Your words?

**16:10** You alone have created the righteous one, and from the womb You have established him

**16:11** for the appointed time of good pleasure, to be kept in Your covenant and to walk in all Your ways,

**16:12** and to [...] upon him in the abundance of Your mercies, and to open all the anguish of his soul

**16:13** to eternal salvation and everlasting peace, and no lack. You have raised his glory

**16:14** above flesh.

**16:15** But the wicked You have created for the time of Your wrath, and from the womb You have set them apart

**16:16** for the day of slaughter. For they walk in the way that is not good,

**16:17** and they have rejected Your covenant, and their soul has loathed Your truth.

**16:18** They have taken no delight in all that You have commanded, and they have chosen what You hate.

**16:19** For according to the mysteries of Your understanding You have [...] all their retribution

**16:20** for Your judgments, to execute judgment in them before all Your works,

**16:21** that they may be a sign and a portent for generations eternal, so that all may know Your glory

**16:22** and Your great power. And what is flesh that it should have insight into these things?

**16:23** And how does the vessel of clay understand wonders? He was in iniquity from the womb,

**16:24** and until old age in the guilt of unfaithfulness. And I know

**16:25** that righteousness does not belong to a mortal, nor to a son of man the way of perfection.

**16:26** To God Most High belong all works of righteousness, and the way of a mortal is not established

**16:27** except by the spirit that God has formed for him, to perfect a way for the sons of men,

**16:28** that all His works may know the strength of His might and the abundance of His mercies

**16:29** upon all the sons of His good pleasure.

**16:30** And as for me, the dread of You has seized me, and trembling and shaking have gripped me,

**16:31** and all my bones have said [...] and my heart has melted like wax before fire,

**16:32** and my knees [...] for I remember my guilt and the unfaithfulness of my ancestors.

**16:33** The wicked have risen against Your covenant, and the worthless against Your word.

**16:34** And I have said: Because of my transgression I am abandoned far from Your covenant.

**16:35** But when I remember the might of Your hand and the multitude of Your mercies, I arise.

**16:36** I stand and my spirit holds fast its station against the blow, for I lean upon Your covenant-faithfulness

**16:37** and the abundance of Your mercies, for You atone for iniquity and purify a mortal from guilt by Your righteousness.

---
*EMET notes: Column 16 closely parallels Column 11 but introduces stark predestinarian language in lines 10-18: the righteous created for good pleasure, the wicked for wrath. This dualistic anthropology is characteristic of the Qumran Instruction on the Two Spirits (1QS III-IV).*
